_about: Unit type vocabulary in PATTERN form. The loader builds a regex per entry at startup: requires_number=true -> \b(<pattern>)\s*(\d{1,4})\b ; requires_number=false -> \b(<pattern>)\b. The matched type+number is captured as ONE unit string. Longest pattern wins (see manifest matching_rules) so 'Brush Engine' is tried before 'Brush'. Adding a unit type = add an entry here, never edit parser code.
_critical_notes: Removal from the working string MUST be case-insensitive (the readout found a case-sensitive str.replace bug — fixed in 4a).
Multi-word and longest-match: 'Brush Engine 6130' must match the 'Brush Engine' entry, not 'Brush' + stray 'Engine 6130'. Sort/try by descending pattern length.
All four directional deputies are NUMBERLESS fixed strings.

unit_types._comment: Brush is TWO distinct units — a brush truck (Brush 702) and a brush engine (Brush Engine 6130). Both valid. Longest-match ensures 'Brush Engine' wins when 'Engine' follows.
All four directional deputies — numberless fixed strings. Code previously had only West/South; North and East were missing.

Missing types found by readout / heard live. NOTE: 'Care' intentionally omitted — it false-positives against 'Crisis Care' (incident type). Add back when a distinct negative-lookbehind pattern is available.
LA appears with AND without a hyphen ('LA-601' and 'LA 608'). Pattern handles the stem; loader should allow optional hyphen/space before the number.

_separator_note: Units are frequently joined by 'and' ('Engine 20 and Rescue 7'). The parser must treat 'and' as a separator, not absorb it into a unit or leave it as a stray token.
